title: Cross-region latency-led capacity snapshots Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a latency-first view of regional GPU capacity for Q3 2026 (Jul–Sep), with snapshots for three demand scenarios and rollout windows for new capacity. The goal is to provide a quick decision artifact for SRE/Capacity leads to prioritize NA/EU/APAC activations when latency SLOs are at risk.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally rough: treat numbers as planning-level (±10%) unless otherwise marked.
- Focus is on tail-latency-sensitive routes (chat/live generation) — not batch embedding/backfill.
- Warmpools here mean kept-warm instances for <50ms cold-starts; counted separately from active fleet.

Executive snapshot (1 line):
- Baseline shows small NA buffer in Jul, EU tight in Aug, APAC at risk in Sep under aggressive demand — recommend reserving a 12% warm buffer in APAC and prioritizing an EU burst window (2 × 8-GPU pods) for calendar week 33.

Interpretation and triggers:
- EU is the first region to hit tail latency pressure under both Baseline and Aggressive scenarios (Aug–Sep). Trigger threshold: tail-99 latency > 120ms for 4h rolling -> open EU burst window.
- APAC shows highest sensitivity due to smaller committed footprint and higher network jitter; aggressive scenario pushes tail-99 to >200ms in Aug/Sep.
- NA has headroom in baseline but aggressive demand consumes that quickly; monitor per-route QPS & model size distribution (L>=32 tokens causes faster KV-cache pressure).

Planned rollout and activation timeline (latency-led prioritization):
- Week 28 (Jul 12–18): Soft-activate EU warmpool + add 2 × 8-GPU pods (reserved commit) — purpose: small-burst capacity for canaries. Owner: Elena.
- Week 31 (Aug 2–8): NA warm capacity increase + enable autoscale-ramp thresholds for chat routes (scale at 65% util instead of 80%). Owner: Samir.
- Week 33 (Aug 16–22): EU burst window hot-standby (2 × 8-GPU on-line for peak) — trigger: tail-99 >120ms sustained 2h OR ticket JIRA-3821 escalated. Owner: Marcus.
- Week 36 (Sep 6–12): APAC reserve commit review & negotiate additional 40 GPUs (spot-to-commit migration) if aggressive scenario signals persist. Owner: Priya.

Operational mitigations (short-list):
- Route-level fallbacks: move chat routes to smaller-context models when tail-99 crosses 150ms for >30m. (Product/Model lead sign-off required).
- Prioritize KV-cache isolation for high-QPS tenants to reduce cross-tenant tail spikes.
- Adjust batcher windows for NA/EU to prefer lower latency (slightly reducing throughput) when 95th latency > configured SLO.
- Temporary traffic shaping: shift non-SLA traffic to lower-priority pool during EU/A PAC peak hours.

Unresolved questions / open items (notes to self):
- Need clearer per-route token-length histograms for EU chat customers (ask telemetry team; ticket created: JIRA-3860).
- Confirm billing impact of moving 40 GPUs from spot to reserved in APAC for a 3-month runway. Finance contact: Zoe (cc in thread).
- Warmpool sizing model needs calibration — current estimate uses 50ms cold-start target; validate against actual 10k live sessions in June load test.

Micro-scenarios and recommended actions (table):
- Scenario: Short synthetic traffic spike (2h, +60% QPS) -> Action: auto-burst EU (2 pods) + reduce NA batch windows -> Recovery target: <45m.
- Scenario: Sustained demand lift (2 weeks, +30% baseline) -> Action: negotiate committed capacity in APAC (40 GPUs) + run model-level offload -> Recovery target: capacity reflect in 7–10 days.
- Scenario: Provider zone outage (one EU zone down) -> Action: route 30% EU traffic to NA on latency-insensitive endpoints, enable cloud-provider fallback and notify customers. Recovery target: restore within 24h with region failover.

Quick checklist before go-ahead:
- [ ] Confirm EU extra pods contracted and billing OK (Finance sign-off)
- [ ] Ops playbook updated with burst activation runbook (SRE owner)
- [ ] Telemetry queries for per-route token-length ready (Telemetry owner)
- [ ] Warm-up scripts validated in staging (Bench infra)

Relevant links and memory hooks:
- Slack thread: #infra-capacity -> thread "eu-latency-23Jul"
- Load test run: gs://redwood-loadtests/2026-06-warmup-eu (notes inside)

Bottom line (recommended):
- Approve EU burst window (week 33) and hold APAC commit decision until Sep 6 review unless aggressive signals appear earlier.
